note: Ceilings for `bun run check:ui` (issue #2580). Recorded from a real run on this machine — see the PR. The floors this lane is FOR are cardsOcc 0, ctrlsStranded 0 and axeSerious/axeCritical 0. AS OF ISSUE #2593 EVERY WALKED SURFACE HOLDS axeSerious 0 / axeCritical 0 — those two are no longer debt lines anywhere, so a nonzero reading is a regression, not a carried defect. The one surface that could not hold it as written is `/admin/design-system`, whose job includes SHOWING what a failing token looks like: its three deliberate specimens carry `data-axe-exempt="<why>"`, the lane excludes those subtrees and prints `exempt<n>` on the surface's line of every run, and `scripts/__tests__/axe-exemption-scope.test.ts` fails if the attribute appears anywhere but that page. An exemption is a named node in a reviewable diff; a nonzero budget row is a number nobody can attribute. Where a surface breaks one of the REMAINING floors today; where a surface breaks one of those TODAY the entry keeps the measured value and carries a `knownDebt` note naming the defect, printed under every run. A slice that fixes a surface lowers its ceilings in the same PR. A surface nobody can walk yet is `{"status":"unwalked","reason":…}` — listed in the output and in the coverage line, never silently green. Issue #2582 (PR #2619) moved the probe's `occ`/`reachable` boundary, and it moved it in BOTH directions. A control is `occ` when the centre of its VISIBLE INTERSECTION with (viewport n its own SCROLL PORT) hit-tests to something else, and `reachable` when that intersection is EMPTY but a gesture can bring it back — see `probe.js`'s `scrollPort` / `probe`. The old rule tested the element's raw centre against the bare viewport. LOOSER than the old rule: a control lying wholly outside its port's box (the deck-builder's off-strip `Delete column MV n` buttons) is no longer `occ`, and neither is one straddling a port's clip edge with a band below it (the lobby's `Your Events (all)` under the new bottom nav) — `<main>` paints nothing there, so nothing can be occluding it. STRICTER than the old rule: a control PARTLY clipped by its port is now hit-tested over the strip it still paints, where a raw centre would have been thrown away as out-of-window (`design-system-dialog`'s section-08 Cancel/Confirm specimens), and a `position: fixed` box gets no port at all rather than borrowing an ancestor scroller's rectangle. Rows re-recorded against the corrected probe carry the measurement and its enumeration in their own note. `deck-builder` was re-recorded whole on 2026-08-20 (issue #2585 fixup, PR #2650): the filter controls leaving the header band for a sheet/popover freed real height at every viewport, and a follow-up fixup (search bar `min-w-0 overflow-hidden`, Filters button icon-only under `short-viewport:`) closed a same-day regression at `844x390x3` where the new Filters button wrapped the header onto two full-height rows and pushed the Maindeck's Delete-column row under `SaveDeckBar` (`ctrlsOcc` 2 → 5 mid-fix → 1 final). Rows not re-recorded still measure below their number and are deliberately left alone, and the notes on them describe debt the surface's own slice owns. Issue #2822 removed the reason those readings used to VARY on the Limited side: every `limited-*` and `draft-*` row is now measured against a seeded, label-addressed fixture (`convex/limitedFixtures.ts`, reached through the `?label=` filter and the row's `data-limited-event-label`), so none of them is a function of how many events this deployment holds or which seat a positional scan landed on. Those seven surfaces were re-recorded WHOLE on 2026-08-26 — their prior viewport blocks were deleted rather than `--accept`ed one cell at a time, because the fixture is a different SUBJECT and an accepted drift would have implied continuity that does not exist. `limited-build` left `unwalked` in the same change: the builder route needs only a dealt, non-empty pool, which the mid-draft fixture seat has. Issue #2658 adds `small`: count of visible in-band interactive controls under 44px on their smaller dimension (`probe.js`'s `smallN`). This key is DELIBERATELY POINTER-BLIND — the probe applies the same 44px test at every viewport, but `--control-h` resolves to 32px under `pointer: fine` ON PURPOSE (`src/index.css:942,946-948`, citing WCAG 2.5.8, a TOUCH-target rule). So the `1440x900x2` (desktop, pointer: fine) row of every surface reads a nonzero `small` that is the intended 32px control height, not debt; the four `…,mobile,touch…` rows (390x844x3, 844x390x3, 820x1180x2, 1180x820x2) read real sub-44px tap-target debt. Every nonzero `small` ceiling below carries a `knownDebt` note saying explicitly which of the two it is — a reader must never "fix" a desktop reading by shrinking a touch target, or dismiss a touch reading as "just the desktop thing". This ticket only RECORDS the touch-viewport debt as a ceiling so it cannot deepen; #2659 owns lowering it. Issue #2724 adds `cardsSquare`: card surfaces that are SQUARE — a card showing page background inside its own rectangle instead of the printed rounded corner (`probe.js`'s `cardsSquareN`). It is a HARD FLOOR of 0 on every surface and must never be raised: the whole point of the proportional `--card-radius` recipe (ADR 0103 §7) is that no card is ever square, and the check exists because happy-dom has no layout and cannot see a shape at all. Measured by COMPUTED RADIUS: the probe walks the card's own box chain (the image plus any ancestor whose rect is the same box), takes the largest `border-top-left-radius` on an element that actually CLIPS to it — the image itself, or an ancestor with non-visible `overflow` or paint containment, since a radius on a non-clipping ancestor does not shape the square art inside it — and reds when that radius is under 2.4% of the card's width, half the printed 4.8% fraction. The threshold is a FRACTION because the token is one: a fixed radius looks right at one card size and wrong at every other. Two mechanisms were tried and rejected, and re-deriving either from this note would rebuild a check that measures nothing. NOT a hit test at the corner (the first implementation, withdrawn): the corner is an ellipse quadrant, so a point inset by `i` on both axes sits outside it only when i < ~0.29·r — ~1.1px on a 78x109 phone deck tile — and `elementFromPoint` takes CSS-pixel coordinates the browser snaps to device pixels, so a sub-pixel inset is not reliably where you put it; it reported `cardsSquare 36` at 390x844x3 on a tree whose cards were all visibly, correctly rounded (screenshot-confirmed). NOT a pixel read: card art is cross-origin, so a canvas read is tainted. The known limit, recorded in `probe.js`: a FIXED radius that happens to land near the right fraction on one small card passes — that case is also visually indistinguishable, and the CSS recipe (`.card-corner` / `.card-ring`) is what holds it.
